About Zeta
Build the future of banking.
Zeta is a next-generation banking technology company providing cloud-native, fully stackable processing and core banking platforms for issuers. With a focus on scalability, compliance, and innovation, Zeta empowers financial institutions to modernize their technology infrastructure and deliver secure, seamless digital banking experiences.
Our impact runs at real-world scale. Today, over 25 million cards are live on Zeta-powered platforms across 7 countries, supported by a passionate team of 1,700+ Zetanauts across India, the US, EMEA, and Asia. Backed by SoftBank Vision Fund, Mastercard, and other reputed strategic investors, we reached a valuation of $2 billion in 2025.
Our focus is on establishing product lines that focus on key outcomes by addressing real customer pain points, modernizing legacy systems, and strengthening core fundamentals. As a result, our systems and platforms support a wide range of banking and payments capabilities, including:
1. Tachyon, our cloud-native banking stack built for population-scale systems
2. Cipher, our unified authentication platform for secure, high-volume banking environments
3. Digital Credit as a Service, enabling banks to launch credit lines on UPI
4. Elena, our intelligent and conversational AI platform for banking
5. Pixel, India’s first digital-native credit card, launched in partnership with HDFC Bank, for whom we also revamped their PayZapp mobile app: Winner of the Celent Model Bank Award for Payments Innovation 2024
6. Sparrow, the leading card experience for non-prime cardholders in the US…and more across cards, payments, lending, and core banking.
We are an engineering-first organization that values ownership, bias for action, and long-term thinking. Together, we solve some of the hardest problems in banking tech. Our culture is built around trust, collaboration, and creating the conditions for you to drive impact proportionate to your potential. Reinforcing our commitment to creating an inclusive and supportive workplace, we have been consistently recognized as a Great Place to Work.
If you want to build cutting-edge banking tech that enables banks to serve millions reliably, securely, and at a population scale, Zeta is your playground.
If you would like to learn more about how we have grown and evolved over the years, watch our journey here. You can also explore our website and follow us on LinkedIn, Instagram,YouTube, and X.
 
About the Product
Zeta is building a new consumer banking product for the US market. The focus is learning fast which features drive adoption, engagement and retention — and building them well.
 
About the Role
You'll help grow the product through a steady cadence of experiments and feature launches. Each PM owns a business-outcome metric for one area of the product, and the roadmap that moves it. Example areas: onboarding and activation, engagement and retention, revenue, and trust and risk.
We need a hustler. The work will feel like a very early-stage startup: ambiguous problems, incomplete information, shifting priorities and no playbook. You'll bring structure to the chaos: find the answers, make the calls and get things shipped.
We expect PMs to use AI tools across the lifecycle — research, specs, prototyping, analysis — to keep iteration cycles short. PMs here go deep on how things are built, so hands-on software development experience is mandatory.


Responsibilities
1. Own a metric

• Own a business-outcome metric for your area, plus the guardrail metrics it must not trade away.

• Keep a ranked backlog of experiments and features, prioritised by expected impact (RICE, ICE or similar).

2. Run experiments

• Write each bet as a hypothesis with a primary metric, guardrails and a decision rule, all set before launch.

• Match the method to the traffic: A/B tests and holdouts at scale; fake doors, usability tests and cohort analysis at low volume.

• Size tests properly, report null and negative results as plainly as wins, and make the ship, iterate or kill call.

• Keep a running log of what was tested, what was learned and what changed.

3. Build features

• Take features from problem definition through spec, build, QA, launch and adoption.

• Write specs engineers can build from: flows, edge cases, failure states, event instrumentation and acceptance criteria.

• Work through technical design with engineering — APIs, data models, ledger and payment flows, third-party integrations — and make trade-off calls quickly.

4. Measure

• Define output metrics (acquisition, activation, revenue, engagement) and the input metrics that drive them (funnel conversion, feature usage).

• Own event instrumentation and data quality for your area.

• Do your own analysis in SQL, product analytics tools (such as Mixpanel, Amplitude or MoEngage) and BI tools (such as Metabase or Superset).

5. Research users

• Run continuous discovery with US customers through remote interviews, usability tests and surveys.

• Turn what you hear and what the data shows into clear problem statements that feed the backlog.

6. Shape the UX

• Partner with designers on simple flows that earn users' trust.

• Own product copy for your area.

7. Launch and support

• Ship behind feature flags and in stages, with monitoring and a rollback plan.

• Work with compliance, risk, banking partners, operations and support so every launch meets regulatory requirements and can be supported from day one.

Skills
• Statistics and experiment design: hypothesis testing, significance, power and sample sizing, and common traps such as peeking and novelty effects.

• Strong SQL, and fluency with product analytics and BI tools.

• Ability to work through messy data sets and turn them into decisions.

• Engineering fundamentals you still use: reading code, system design, APIs and data models.

• A keen eye for design, and strong UX writing.

• Clear written and verbal communication — specs and experiment readouts people can act on.

• Meticulous program management across parallel workstreams.

• Hands-on experience with user research.

Experience and Qualifications
• 6+ years of total experience, including: 3–4 years in product management, with features shipped and measured in production. At least 3 years of hands-on software development, writing and shipping production code as an engineer. This is mandatory.

• A track record of experiments that changed a product decision.

• Preferred: consumer fintech, payments or banking experience, ideally in the US.

• Preferred: B2C products with a growth or experimentation focus.

9b4be0c755fd255c.description: Start your career in finance with Morgan Stanley as a Investment Banking Analyst Intern in Thiruvananthapuram. You will sit with a working investment bank team, use the same systems and reports they do, and own a defined piece of work from day one. About the role As a Investment Banking Analyst Intern at Morgan Stanley, your core focus will be financial modelling, valuation and pitch-book preparation for live deals. You will be attached to a named mentor, join the team's daily stand-ups and reviews, and be trusted with work that genuinely matters rather than filing and formatting. Questions are encouraged, mistakes are treated as teaching moments, and your output is reviewed properly so you actually improve. What you'll do day to day Support financial modelling, valuation and pitch-book preparation for live deals alongside the core investment bank team Work in Excel and the company's internal systems on live financial data Prepare schedules, reconciliations and reports that go to real reviewers Research companies, customers, products or regulations as the work demands Turn your analysis into clear notes and decks for senior stakeholders Follow the documentation and control standards a regulated business requires Take part in reviews, ask questions and act on the feedback you receive Skills you'll build You will build practical, demonstrable experience in Financial Modelling, Valuation (DCF & Comparables), MS Excel, PowerPoint / Pitch Books, Company Research, M&A Fundamentals, Accounting Fundamentals, Capital Markets, Analytical Thinking, Business Writing the exact toolkit that separates a hireable finance fresher from a CV full of coursework. No prior work experience is required. Curiosity, numerical comfort and care with detail matter far more here than a polished rsum, and every one of these skills is taught on the job. Who should apply Students in their final year or recent graduates from MBA (Finance)/CFA L1/CA/B.Com (Hons)/BBA based in or willing to work from Thiruvananthapuram. You should be comfortable with numbers, willing to learn Financial Modelling, Valuation (DCF & Comparables), MS Excel, and able to communicate clearly in writing. Relevant coursework, certifications (NISM, CFA L1, GST, Tally) or a strong academic record in Financial Modelling will strengthen your application, but none of them are mandatory. Internship details This is a 3-month internship in Thiruvananthapuram, Kerala, with a stipend of 43,000 per month. You will be given a defined project so that you leave with a valuation model and pitch deck for a real transaction. Working hours follow the team's normal business hours and the internship includes a certificate on successful completion. You will finish this internship able to read a set of financial statements with confidence, work comfortably in Excel at speed, and explain exactly how your work fed a real business decision. Strong performers are considered for a Pre-Placement Offer (PPO) and a full-time role. How to apply Click Apply Now. If you are not logged in you will be asked to sign in and register first, after which you will be taken to Morgan Stanley's official careers page to complete your application. Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis and seats for this Financial Modelling-focused internship are limited, so apply early. Responsibilities: Support financial modelling, valuation and pitch-book preparation for live deals alongside the core investment bank team; Work in Excel and internal systems on live financial data; Prepare schedules, reconciliations and reports for senior review; Research companies, customers, products or regulations as required; Present analysis clearly in notes and decks for stakeholders; Follow documentation and control standards required in a regulated business. Requirements: Pursuing or recently completed MBA (Finance)/CFA L1/CA/B.Com (Hons)/BBA 2026 freshers & final-year students welcome; Working knowledge of Financial Modelling, Valuation (DCF & Comparables), MS Excel (or a genuine willingness to learn them); Strong numerical ability and comfort working in MS Excel; Care with detail and the discipline to document work properly; Clear written and verbal communication in English; Based in or willing to work from Thiruvananthapuram, Kerala. .

ODK | Senior Product Manager | Remote (Worldwide) | Long-term contract, 30–40 hours/week | $90–$110/hour USD
ODK is an open-source platform used by thousands of organizations worldwide to collect billions of data points for disease surveillance, supply chain traceability, environmental monitoring, and more. It enables users to build powerful forms and reliably collect structured data, even in places with little or no Internet connectivity.
ODK has been actively developed for 18 years. We have a mix of self-hosted and SaaS users across many sectors. We're looking for a senior product manager who will own product discovery and prioritization across this diverse user base. To be successful, you'll need to find the common needs behind very different workflows and turn them into opinionated product improvements.
Because the team is small and the user base is large, this is a high-autonomy role where product decisions have an unusually direct impact. You should have substantial experience managing complex B2B or technical products. Experience with open source, self-hosted software, and small, fully remote teams is a plus.
Details and application: https://getodk.org/about/jobs/senior-product-manager
